checks: For an old proper section, project nearby sections to the old section plane. Compactness gives containment in arbitrarily small neighborhoods of the old section for small displacements, while convex combinations with an interior point on the appropriate side give translated scaled copies with scale tending to one. This establishes two-sided area continuity. Strict full or empty cuts have no nearby sections, and a zero-area supporting section has zero inside limit by the same compactness upper bound and zero area outside.

Linear coarea therefore gives old mass change −tsS_ij with uniform o(t) on bounded s, and each source section gives a strictly positive coarea contribution. The divisor is the Euclidean norm of the continuous normal because the threshold moves in the scalar cap coordinate.

At a proper section, any supporting plane at a relative-interior section point would contain the section plane and contradict its crossing of the interior. Thus the proper plane meets the boundary in a surface-null set. Zero-area support is also surface-null and strict cuts have empty plane trace. Off the old plane the old cap indicator is eventually constant uniformly on the signed O(t) shell and bounded threshold speeds. The radial bound and dominated convergence give the fixed captured-boundary loss uniformly; the interval case uses endpoint counting and a proper interior section.

At mass Q+tη, offsets s=−(L_ij+η)/S_ij plus or minus any fixed positive increment give uniformly opposite mass residuals on bounded η. The strictly decreasing local inverse therefore has the stated uniform expansion without differentiability away from the old threshold.

Since B_i>0, two bounded opposite η brackets contain the scalar solution for small t, giving q_i(t)−Q=O(t). Substitution gives q_i′=−∑θ_ij L_ij−α_i′/B_i. Using M_t=M−tD+o(t) contributes +βD/M to the normalized derivative. Finitely many strict derivative inequalities on the same path make the finite covering upper bound strictly below β.

As a direct sign check on [−(1−ht),1−ht] in the invariant buffer, each Γ-unit normal has S=1/√3, L=h and the contact coefficient is εh. The formula gives q_i′=−h(1+ε/√3) and zero normalized derivative, matching the exact mass ratio.
